question: Under paragraph 10 and footnote 1 of 26EC22, what would justify concluding that the Product Provider has retained responsibility and fulfilled the requirement? Distinguish allocation of authority, supervisory conduct and operational or record-keeping outcomes. What remains unresolved without an applicable standard and actual facts?

26EC22:10.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

26EC22:11.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

26EC22:12.quote: Product Providers should have appropriate measures in place to manage and mitigate cybersecurity risks3, data privacy, system outages and recovery, and maintain a comprehensive and robust business continuity plan.

26EC22:FN1.quote: 1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

UT-Code:6.8.quote: 6.8 The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.

reasoning.text: Paragraph 10 leaves ultimate responsibility for management, operational soundness and ownership record keeping with the Product Provider despite outsourcing. Footnote 1 repeats full responsibility and explains why records reflecting investors’ ownership matter. An appointment allocates performance; it does not itself discharge this responsibility.

The retained Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds 6.8 requires a register maintained by the scheme, trustee or person appointed by the trustee. Footnote 1 expressly preserves the Product Provider’s responsibility despite such arrangements. Section I Handbook 6.8 concerns Product Key Facts Statements and supplies no outsourcing rule. Edition and applicability still require review.

Proper records of ownership, operational compatibility, appropriate risk measures and a robust continuity plan concern conduct and results as well as responsibility allocation. A supervision or reconciliation event is evidence relevant to these requirements, but proof that the event occurred does not establish its adequacy.

As a logical counterexample, two records may agree because both copied the same mistaken owner. Agreement then establishes consistency without establishing the ownership interest that the records should reflect. The legal account needs constitutive terms, rights, parties and record provenance, alongside reconciliation evidence.

The strongest narrower reading treats paragraph 10 principally as allocation of responsibility, leaving the content of particular standards to paragraph 11, other applicable requirements and the arrangement. A stronger conduct or outcome reading needs those additional warrants. The retained wording does not by itself establish strict liability for every operational defect, or a universal deadline or action that cures a breach.

conditions.then: Ultimate responsibility remains with the Product Provider under the retained wording; fulfillment still needs assessment.

conditions.if: Records match but identify the wrong owner
conditions.then: Matching cannot establish proper ownership records; investigate the shared error and the governing rights.

conditions.if: A defect and a remedy are documented
conditions.then: Assess the remedy against the applicable duty and facts; no universal cure rule has been established.

facts_required: Applicable product code and source edition; provider/trustee/delegate roles and constitutive terms.
Delegation powers, monitoring access, incident chronology and actual remedial decisions.
Which record constitutes or evidences ownership; reconciliation design and independent title evidence.
remaining_limits: No complete individual fulfillment review of the original obligations/readings.
No established general liability or cure standard beyond the inspected wording.
